Introduction

Zika virus (ZIKV) is an arbovirus belonging to the family Flaviviridae, and is closely related to the dengue, yellow fever, Japanese encephalitis, and West Nile viruses. It was first isolated from a monkey in the Zika forest of Uganda in 1947

ZIKV is primarily transmitted by the bites of infectious Aedes mosquitoes

With the ease of modern transportation, there is a potential that the ZIKV outbreak may become a global public health crisis.

In this work, we present a compartmental model for ZIKV based on SEIR host model and SEI vector model, using logistic growth in human population and dynamic vector population

Method and Design

The compartmental model consists of two parts: the compartments for human, subscripted with 𝐻𝐻; and compartments for vectors, subscripted with 𝑉𝑉. Although there have been a few reported deaths related to ZIKV, most ZIKV cases only result in mild symptoms among infectious individuals. We use an SEIR (Susceptible, Exposed, Infectious, Recovered) model to describe the disease spread among the human population. Let 𝑆𝑆 𝐻𝐻 (𝑡𝑡), 𝐸𝐸 𝐻𝐻 (𝑡𝑡), 𝐼𝐼 𝐻𝐻 (𝑡𝑡) and 𝑅𝑅 𝐻𝐻 (𝑡𝑡) denote the number of individuals in each compartment at time 𝑡𝑡. The human population at time t is given as 𝑁𝑁 𝐻𝐻 (𝑡𝑡) = 𝑆𝑆 𝐻𝐻 (𝑡𝑡) + 𝐼𝐼 𝐻𝐻 (𝑡𝑡) + 𝐸𝐸 𝐻𝐻 (𝑡𝑡) + 𝑅𝑅 𝐻𝐻 (𝑡𝑡). During the outbreak, the human population is assumed to follow a logistic growth with carrying capacity 𝐾𝐾 𝐻𝐻 .

The compartments for vectors consist of both the infectious status and the life stages of the mosquito. In particular, a typical life cycle of a mosquito has four stages: egg, larva, pupa, and adult. Let 𝑉𝑉 1 (𝑡𝑡), 𝑉𝑉 2 (𝑡𝑡) and 𝑉𝑉 3 (𝑡𝑡) denote the number of eggs, larvae, and pupae of vectors in the environment. Since only female adults bite humans and transmit the virus, there are no infectious compartments for these three stages.
